what_starts_a_draft_today.in_words: The resident worker sends the closed message analysis_ready{tenant, request_id} to the queue named by env IRPT_ANALYSIS_READY_QUEUE_URL once, right after it has written the job state READY (mark_ready -> signal_ready -> send_ready), and again on a redelivery of an already-READY job that has no i3_sent_at marker. THE CONDITION IS NOT 'the job is bound to a ticket id': mark_ready copies ticket_id into the READY receipt when the accepted record carries one, but it calls signal_ready on every path; the only guard inside send_ready is that the queue-url env var is non-empty (empty -> one WARN and no send). A job with no ticket_id sends too (test_ready_signal.py test_b, run offline here: 2 passed). RECEIVER: the commentary Lambda admits only the byte-exact closed message (admit_ready_message), builds a READY item from tenant + request_id alone, reads the composition through the svc-commentary reader (which refuses unless the job row reads READY), and, when a model is configured and no draft is stored yet, drafts, stores the draft and sends commentary_ready. It reads no ticket_id and no commentary member anywhere on that path.

submission.in_words: No member of a submission says commentary is asked for. The browser body is a CLOSED set: validate_public_request refuses any key outside PUBLIC_FIELDS = {request_id, client_id, account_ids, snapshot_id, variant, comparison_keys, report_title, prepared_for, input_id, ticket_id} (UNKNOWN_OR_SERVER_OWNED_FIELD) and the published schema is additionalProperties false. The nearest member is ticket_id, which says only that the request was filed under a ticket (it must come with input_id and match TCK-yyyymmdd-xxxxxxxx); from it commentary could only be INFERRED, and no code on the send path makes that inference. The intake stores the validated browser in the retained composition (document.browser) and its hash as record.browser_sha256, so a stored copy carries the same closed set. Nothing here is a member; all of it is a statement about absence.

ticket.in_words: The ticket DOES have a field for it: answers.add_commentary, a boolean on an analysis_request ticket (true = a commentary asked for; false or omitted = a report only). It is declared in the ticket service's TYPE_DEFINITIONS (the ticket project's contract is that code; no separate schema file or TCKT PRD text names it) and validated at create. NO code in the IRPT tree reads it: the submission carries only ticket_id, the worker, the acceptance writer and the commentary receiver never fetch a ticket, and the only reader anywhere in this repo is the drafter's own ticket_client self-check on a ticket it writes. Whether the portal's ticket form sets it is not established (the portal submodule is not checked out here).

accepted_record.in_words: The ACCEPTED record is the immutable JSON attribute `record` on the item {tenant, request_revision = 'analysis#<request_id>#1'} of the irpt-requests table, written exactly once by DynamoAcceptance.accept in one transact_write together with the job row (condition attribute_not_exists). A replayed submit returns the prior record exactly as stored (accept :108-110, :135-139), so a member added to the writer later is absent on every record accepted before it, permanently. SIBLING, NOT MEMBER: commentary_ref is set later by the draft store as a separate attribute of the same item ('SET commentary_ref', conditional update), and DynamoAcceptance.get returns only the `record` attribute.

acceptance_could_read_it.from_what: Nothing in hand at the writing line says it. DynamoAcceptance.accept receives owner, browser, composition_ref, ingestion_revision, destination_revision and acting_principal_id. `browser` is the validated submission, whose closed member set has no commentary member and whose only related member is ticket_id (an id, not a ticket body). acceptance.py imports no ticket client, takes no ticket port and makes no ticket call. The only place the asked-for fact exists today is the ticket's answers.add_commentary, so reading it at acceptance would be a ticket read, which the CTO has ruled out for the worker and the drafter.
